text: How CI enforces it How CI enforces it scripts/run-rule-probes.sh analyses both trees and runs scripts/check_rule_probes.py . It prints one PAIR OK line per rule and exits non-zero if a positive probe fires zero times or twice, or if a clean twin fires once. Reintroducing a defect into a clean twin therefore fails the run and names the rule.

text: aem-dead-006 missingtranslationkey translation key used by a template or model has no entry in the baseline (en) dictionary. dead-code i18n htl warning add the key to the baseline en.json dictionary (and to every other locale), or correct the key at the use site. aem prints the raw key when ${'key' @ i18n} has no dictionary entry, so a missing translation ships to production as visible text. the build and the bundle both pass, and the only signal is a customer reading "checkout.title" on the page. keeping every locale in step by hand also guarantees that the en dictionary silently drifts …
title: AEM-DEAD-006 MissingTranslationKey

text: aem-dead-007 brokenhtlinclude htl data-sly-include target is missing or forms an include cycle. dead-code htl warning correct the include path to an existing template, or break the include cycle. sightly resolves data-sly-include while rendering, so a renamed or mis-pathed include is invisible to the build. it surfaces only as an empty region on one page, long after the template was moved. an include cycle is worse: rendering recurses until the request is aborted. correct the include path to an existing template relative to the including file, or break the cycle by factoring the shared markup …
title: AEM-DEAD-007 BrokenHtlInclude

text: aem-dup-001 duplicateservletendpoint multiple osgi servlets claim identical paths or resourcetypes/selectors/methods without ranking distinction. duplication error merge the servlets or add distinct selectors/resource types. two servlets that answer the same request make the response depend on registration order and service ranking. on a publish tier the result can differ between instances, which is the hardest class of bug to reproduce. merge the servlets, or give each one a distinct contract: a different resource type, selectors, extension or http method. reach for an explicit …
title: AEM-DUP-001 DuplicateServletEndpoint

text: aem-dup-002 duplicateosgiconfiguration conflicting or duplicate osgi configuration targeting the same pid in the same runmode context. duplication warning keep one config per pid and runmode; remove the duplicate. two files configuring the same pid in the same runmode context are both installed and the winner depends on install order. values then differ between a fresh install and an incremental one — the classic "works on my instance" configuration bug. keep exactly one file per pid and runmode context and merge the properties into it. split by runmode (config, config.author, config.publish) …
title: AEM-DUP-002 DuplicateOsgiConfiguration

text: aem-dup-003 duplicateslingmodel multiple sling models bind to the exact same resourcetype and adapter interface without condition. duplication warning differentiate the resourcetype/adapters or merge the models. two sling models bound to the same resourcetype and adaptable means htl can resolve either one; the winner is undefined. exported json then differs depending on which model the model factory picked. keep one model per resource type, or separate them by selector, resource type or a condition, and let htl choose explicitly. dup
title: AEM-DUP-003 DuplicateSlingModel

text: aem-dup-010 duplicatecodeblock duplicate java code block or method clone detected across repository classes. duplication warning extract the duplicated block into a shared helper. cloned code drifts: a fix applied to one copy silently misses the others, and every copy has to be re-tested. duplication across bundles is usually a missing shared module. extract the duplicated block into a helper or an interface in the bundle that already owns the concept, and have both call sites use it. dup
title: AEM-DUP-010 DuplicateCodeBlock

text: aem-perf-001 unclosedresourceresolver resourceresolver obtained via factory is not closed in try-with-resources or finally. performance error wrap the resolver in try-with-resources. a resolver obtained from the factory and never closed keeps its jcr session and its caches alive for the life of the jvm. aem as a cloud service logs leaked resolvers and eventually refuses new ones, so the instance degrades instead of failing fast. always obtain the resolver in a try-with-resources block, or close it in a finally block, and never hand it to another thread. perf
title: AEM-PERF-001 UnclosedResourceResolver

text: aem-perf-002 unclosedjcrsession jcr session obtained via repository login or adaptation is not logged out or closed. performance error close the owning resolver or call session.logout() in a finally block. a jcr session opened through repository.login() or adapted from a resolver must be logged out. an open session pins the observation queue and any pending changes, and on aem as a cloud service leaked sessions show up as repository connection pressure. close the session in a finally block, or avoid the session entirely: the resource resolver api covers almost every read and write a component …
title: AEM-PERF-002 UnclosedJcrSession

text: aem-perf-003 oakquerytraversalrisk jcr-sql2 or xpath query lacks path or nodetype restriction, causing oak traversal errors. performance warning add a path or nodetype restriction to the query. a jcr-sql2 or xpath query with no path or node type restriction forces oak to walk every index it has. at scale that is the difference between a millisecond lookup and a traversal warning in the cloud service logs. add a path= or type= constraint (or isdescendantnode) so oak can use a property index, and confirm the index exists. perf
title: AEM-PERF-003 OakQueryTraversalRisk

text: aem-perf-004 unboundedquery jcr/oak query has no limit and may scan an unbounded result set. performance query warning add a result limit (p.limit / query limit) to bound the query. an unbounded query result can be enormous on a content repository that grows daily. it is the usual cause of a slow component that only shows up in production. bound the result set with p.limit (or limit in jcr-sql2) and paginate with p.offset. report the total separately with p.guesstotal rather than materialising every hit. perf
title: AEM-PERF-004 UnboundedQuery

text: aem-qual-001 pathboundservletregistration sling servlet registered using paths instead of resource types (cqbp-75). quality aem-cloud warning register the servlet by resourcetype instead of paths (cqbp-75). cqbp-75 cloud manager's cqbp-75 rejects path-bound servlets because they bypass sling's resource-centric security model and cannot be dispatched or cached like a resource. they also break the dispatcher rules teams rely on for /content urls. register the servlet by resourcetype and address it through a resource, with selectors and extensions for the variants. for a redirect or a download …
title: AEM-QUAL-001 PathBoundServletRegistration

text: aem-qual-002 providertypeimplementation custom code implements or extends @providertype product interface (cqbp-84). quality aem-cloud error implement only consumer-facing apis; do not implement @providertype (cqbp-84). cqbp-84 implementing or extending a @providertype interface ties your bundle to product internals that aem as a cloud service upgrades without notice; cqbp-84 fails the build for exactly this reason. provider types are contracts you consume, not implement. depend on the interface and delegate to it instead of implementing it. when you need to decorate behaviour, wrap the …
title: AEM-QUAL-002 ProviderTypeImplementation

text: aem-qual-003 slingschedulerusage sling whiteboard scheduler used instead of sling scheduled jobs (amscore-554). quality aem-cloud warning use sling scheduled jobs instead of the whiteboard scheduler (amscore-554). amscore-554 amscore-554 flags the sling whiteboard scheduler. aem as a cloud service expects sling scheduled jobs, which are cluster-aware: a job runs once across the publish tier instead of once per instance, and it survives a restart. implement a jobconsumer for the topic and schedule the run through the sling job api instead of scheduler.addjob. qual
title: AEM-QUAL-003 SlingSchedulerUsage

text: aem-qual-004 unsafecomponentstate non-thread-safe or session-bound object stored in osgi component field (aem-3). quality aem-cloud error do not store session-bound or non-thread-safe objects in component fields. aem-3 slinghttpservletrequest, resourceresolver and jcr session are bound to one thread and one request. stored in a component field, they leak across requests: closed resolvers are reused, sessions go stale after a restart, and the component is no longer thread-safe (cloud manager check aem-3). keep only immutable, thread-safe collaborators in fields. obtain request-scoped objects …
title: AEM-QUAL-004 UnsafeComponentState

text: aem-qual-005 administrativeaccessusage deprecated administrative login or resource resolver api used; rejected on aem as a cloud service. quality aem-cloud error use a dedicated service user with a mapped subservice (amscore-553). administrative logins and loginadministrative bypass every permission check and are rejected by aem as a cloud service. they also hide the real acls a feature needs. create a dedicated service user with a serviceusermapper mapping and request a service resource resolver for that subservice, then grant the service user exactly the permissions the feature needs. qual
title: AEM-QUAL-005 AdministrativeAccessUsage

text: aem-qual-006 resolverstoredincomponentfield osgi component stores a request-scoped resourceresolver or jcr session in an instance field. quality resource-lifecycle warning do not store request-scoped resolvers or sessions in component fields; obtain them per request and close them. storing a request-scoped resolver or session in an osgi component field keeps one request's state alive for every later request, which leaks resolvers and can serve stale content. obtain the resolver or session per request and close it in the same scope. the thread-safety owner for this check is aem-qual-004 …
title: AEM-QUAL-006 ResolverStoredInComponentField

text: aem-qual-007 unregistrableslingmodel sling model injects a request-only type or @requestattribute without declaring a request adaptable. quality sling-models warning declare slinghttpservletrequest (or httpservletrequest) among the model's adaptables, or inject the value from the resource instead. sling models resolves an injection against the adaptable, not against the request the adaptable came from. a model declared adaptables = resource.class therefore cannot inject a request, a response or a @requestattribute: the class compiles, the bundle activates and the model registers, then …
title: AEM-QUAL-007 UnregistrableSlingModel

text: aem-qual-008 unprovidedmandatoryreference mandatory @reference target is declared by project sources but registered by no component. quality osgi error register a @component service implementation for the target type, or mark the @reference optional if activation must not depend on it. a declarative services component with an unsatisfied mandatory reference never activates. the bundle stays active and the code compiles because the target type is on the classpath, so the failure is invisible until the servlet 404s or the scheduled job never fires. register an implementation with …
title: AEM-QUAL-008 UnprovidedMandatoryReference

text: aem-sec-001 unsafehtlcontextbypass htl expression uses @ context='unsafe' bypassing xss protection. security xss error remove context='unsafe' and use a properly escaped context. context='unsafe' switches off htl's contextual escaping, and the expression is written into the page verbatim. with any author-controlled or request-derived value that is a stored xss hole (cwe-79) on a publish tier. drop unsafe and let htl pick the context from the surrounding markup. when you really must emit markup, use context='html' and pass it through a sanitiser such as the granite xss api. sec
title: AEM-SEC-001 UnsafeHtlContextBypass

text: aem-sec-002 openredirectorssrf user-controlled input flows into a redirect or outbound http request. security ssrf warning validate redirects and outbound urls against an allowlist; never pass request parameters directly. a request parameter that reaches sendredirect or an outbound http call lets an attacker choose the destination: an open redirect for phishing, or server-side request forgery against internal services (cwe-601). validate the destination against an allowlist of hosts or a fixed set of relative paths before redirecting, and never build an outbound url from unvalidated input. sec
title: AEM-SEC-002 OpenRedirectOrSsrf

text: aem-wf-001 unresolvedworkflowreference workflow launcher points at a model, or a process step at a class, that the project does not ship. workflow content warning point the launcher at a model the project ships (or an existing out-of-the-box model), and the process step at a class that exists in a bundle the project deploys. a workflow launcher references its model by path and a process step references its class by name; both are plain strings in .content.xml. rename the model or move the class and nothing complains at deploy time - the launcher simply never starts, and the workflow that …
title: AEM-WF-001 UnresolvedWorkflowReference
